name: Narrative Binding
description: Integration of temporal sequences into coherent episodes with causal and intentional structure. Proposed mechanism: brain binds events into narratives for memory, planning, and social communication. Neural correlates emerging; computational theory underdeveloped.
key_references: Hasson, U., Chen, J., & Honey, C. J. (2015). Hierarchical process memory: A neurobiological model of structured sequence learning and prediction. bioRxiv, 32447.
Gazzaniga, M. S. (2000). The new cognitive neurosciences. MIT Press.
empirical_evidence: fMRI: listening to narratives engages temporal, parietal, and prefrontal regions (Hasson et al.). Inter-subject synchronization of brain activity across narratives. Memory for events better when organized narratively. TPJ lesions impair theory of mind narratives. Causal role for binding unclear; could be post-hoc organization during retrieval.
